verdictStatement: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. The equality test passes by == on the whole object: namedCorpusWhenFixturesExist matches live G21 v3 with all five keys in order, and the ten live-cell tokens, eleven CCs, three NTs, one FC and four does-not-execute NTs are each carried character-equal. Because every list appears three times in this artifact, I tested all three copies against live and against each other; all agree, with no drift — that redundancy was the sharpest place a partial edit could hide. G21 v3 has no namedCorpusClasses object, so the five lists are the entire corpus surface in the source and this is a complete carry rather than a thin one. Zero identifiers are invented: every CC, NT and FC token in the file is a member of a live list. NT-3, NT-5, NT-4 and NT-7 appear only in the does-not-execute list with executedHere false, and the artifact contains no outcome, result, trace, passed or failed token anywhere. The DR-102 handling is right on the substance, not just the disclaimer: the live DR-102 row is SATISFIED and itself records that hostile-conformance execution remains condition 4 / DR-G21 and is not architecture SATISFIED evidence, so naming CC-1..CC-11 as unauthored G21 corpus restates the live standing rather than disturbing it. All cited digests measure equal with zero mismatches, recordedInputs.HEAD agrees with the top-level head and live HEAD, closure is structurally unavailable with no closure-style field and OBL-DOCTOR-FX-AUTHORING still leftoverDesign true in the cited join, required-now is 26, no DR-G* row is added, and the subject did not move. Four further refutations of my own — drift between redundant copies, an unrecorded standing imported by citing join v4, overstated cited standings, and a smuggled D9 or recipe — all failed against live bytes.
